items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: I remember the Calloway band around those years, ‘44, ‘45, so it must have been Milt

ctx.x: Yeah, I was just over there and played some with Ralph Sutton, he’s a fine player. I also did some things with the Summit Reunion, you know I played with them twenty years ago, Davern and Wilber. They’re fun to play with, did the Bern Jazz Festival, did five concerts, they’re good to play with. I mean a lot of guys are good to play with. I mean if I went through the catalogue, usually of course I try to bring the guys I work with. Like I like Greg. Greg Cohen’s wonderful because he plays acoustic bass. He’s one —…

York has a couple, two or three unplugged bass players. I mean really unplugged. They really play acoustic bass with gut strings. And it’s like fifty years ago. It’s wonderful because the souped up bass and acoustic guitar never really quite hit it off like totally acoustic. There’s also a factor of resistance in the guitar, when you have to work at it, and do this. You know when it’s amplified you have a little tiny pick and you have a light action, the strings lie close to the fingerboard, you don’t have to…
They must have had some endurance.
